summary: Across the texts, Detransitive 1 ranges from physical visibility and emergence to recognizability and impersonal seeming. These meanings are already explicit in its inherited gloss; negative visibility does not require a separate 'disappear' sense.
Active II with ruḥo denotes deliberate self-identification; Detransitive examples omit an external revealer. With appearing before people, ʕal- marks an audience, not an agent.

Impersonal komibayən introduces inferred propositions, sometimes with an L-suffix experiencer (36/36). The masculine form before i rabuṯo at 82/19 may belong to this construction rather than simple feminine agreement.
Part. Pass. covers known/prominent people, specified days and recognizable places; negative plural mbayne in 77/99 supplies a clear state predicate.
PrS 74/112 has contracted kmiban beside plural kmibayni; Talay 1/352 has miban, already represented by inherited LB 352. Prefix variation alone does not establish a new stem.
The sole compact occurrence, PrS 33/62, lacks its verse and is retained only provisionally without an example.
Verify the inherited citation prs 57/13: its nošo lo mbayən sentence matches the supplied PrS 24/30. Could these be different numbering systems?
Is kombayən ono at 78/10 an interrupted impersonal clause, as the German suggests, or a first-person form without its ending?
At 82/19, is i rabuṯo the subject with default agreement, or part of an impersonal assessment?
Do the editors intend predicative mbayən yo at 113/121 and 113/179 to be filed consistently as Part. Pass.? The supplied analyses disagree.
